lixābundus lixa,
I.journeying at pleasure: iter libere ac prolixe faciens, Paul. ex Fest. p. 116 Müll.; cf.: “lixabundus ambulat, qui voluptatis causā ambulat, Gloss. Isid.: Pinacium tam lixabundum currere,” Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 15 Fleck.; v. Ritschl ad h. l.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
